features.source: Seminole country as the interior of the peninsula rather than its coastline: the Apalachee and Alachua prairies where Creek migrants and others settled from the mid-eighteenth century, running down the central ridge to Big Cypress and the Everglades margin that later became the refuge. Deliberately drawn inside the colonial Florida shape, which follows the coast — the people and the claim are not the same boundary. The span ends with the Third Seminole War in 1858, after which the United States forced most Seminoles west; people who remained found refuge in the Everglades. The bands did not constitute a state, even while Spain and then the United States claimed Florida.
